body:
# Artistry

**Artifact + Registry** - A SQLite-based datastore that lets disparate libraries and applications register their data needs and coexist harmoniously in a single database.

## Core Concepts

- **Registry** - Plugins register artifact kinds with schemas; each gets a unique short code (E for "event", U for "user", etc.)
- **Unified Identity** - Global auto-increment IDs across all artifacts, addressable via slugs like `E42`
- **JSON Payload** - Flexible schema stored as JSON, with expression indexes for performance
- **Schema Validation** - JSON Schema subset with type checking, constraints, defaults, and optional fields
- **COW Versioning** - Updates create new versions by default; full history preserved
- **Links** - Cross-reference any artifact to any other with typed relations (auto-deleted with CASCADE)

## Installation

Add to your `shard.yml`:

```yaml
dependencies:
  artistry:
    github: trans/artistry
```

Then run `shards install`.

## Usage

### Setup

```crystal
require "artistry"

# Open database (creates tables if needed)
Artistry.open("myapp.db")

# Or use an existing DB connection (Artistry won't close it)
Artistry.open(existing_db)
```

### Register Artifact Kinds

Schemas use a JSON Schema subset (powered by the [Jargon](https://github.com/trans/jargon) library):

```crystal
Artistry::Registry.register(
  kind: "event",
  plugin: "myapp",
  schema: {
    type: "object",
    properties: {
      title:    {type: "string", minLength: 1},
      date:     {type: "string", format: "date"},
      priority: {type: "integer", minimum: 1, maximum: 5},
      status:   {type: "string", enum: ["draft", "confirmed"], default: "draft"},
    },
    required: ["title", "date"],
    additionalProperties: false,
  },
  description: "Calendar events",
  symbol: "📅",                 # optional emoji for display
  index: ["title", ["date", "priority"]]  # a field, or fields in order (see Indexes)
)
# => "E" (assigned code)
```

### Supported Schema Keywords

| Category | Keywords |
|----------|----------|
| **Type** | `type` (`string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`, `null`) |
| **Object** | `properties`, `required`, `additionalProperties` |
| **String** | `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, `format` |
| **Number** | `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf` |
| **Array** | `items`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `uniqueItems` |
| **General** | `enum`, `const`, `default`, `description` |
| **Composition** | `$ref`, `$defs` |

Fields listed in `required` must be present. Fields not in `required` are optional. Use `default` to provide fallback values (applied on create and update, stored in artifact data). Set `additionalProperties: false` to reject unknown fields. An omitted `type` is inferred from `properties` (object) or `items` (array).

A schema that can't be parsed, such as one declaring `type: "string"` alongside `properties`, or with an invalid `pattern`, raises `Artistry::InvalidSchema` at registration.

### Create Artifacts

```crystal
# status defaults to "draft", priority is optional
event = Artistry::Artifact.create("event", {
  title: "Team Meeting",
  date: "2025-06-15",
})

event.slug       # => "E1"
event.id         # => 1
event["title"]   # => "Team Meeting" (as JSON::Any)
event["status"]  # => "draft" (applied from default)
```

### Validation

```crystal
# Invalid type - raises ValidationError
Artistry::Artifact.create("event", {title: 123, date: "2025-06-15"})
# => ValidationError: title: expected string, got integer

# Constraint violation
Artistry::Artifact.create("event", {title: "", date: "2025-06-15"})
# => ValidationError: title: must be at least 1 characters

# Unknown field rejected (when additionalProperties: false)
Artistry::Artifact.create("event", {title: "Test", date: "2025-06-15", extra: "x"})
# => ValidationError: extra: additionalProperties is false
```

### Query

```crystal
# By ID
Artistry::Artifact.find(1)

# By slug
Artistry::Artifact.find("E1")

# By kind
Artistry::Artifact.where("E")

# With conditions
Artistry::Artifact.where("E", priority: 1)
```

### Indexes

Without an index, `where` with conditions reads every artifact of the kind.
An index lists fields in order. A `where` that fixes its leading fields,
or all of them, reads just that range of it, so a lookup you make often
can take microseconds where a scan takes tens of milliseconds:

```crystal
# Any plugin can ask for an index on any kind, for its own common lookups
Artistry::Registry.add_index("event", ["date", "priority"], plugin: "calendar")

Artistry::Artifact.where("E", date: "2025-06-15")                # leading field
Artistry::Artifact.where("E", date: "2025-06-15", priority: 1)   # both
```

Indexes are shared. A plugin asking for fields that are already indexed is
recorded as wanting that index too, and the index stays until every plugin
that asked for it has dropped it. `register(index:)` asks on the
registering plugin's behalf.

```crystal
Artistry::Registry.indexes("event")      # each index's fields and plugins
Artistry::Registry.drop_index("event", ["date", "priority"], plugin: "calendar")
```

Indexes cover current versions only, so `where(..., include_superseded: true)`
reads every version. A field is a name of letters, digits, `_` and `-`,
with `.` between nested names (`meta.author`); anything else raises
`Artistry::InvalidIndex`.

SQLite chooses which index a query uses from statistics it keeps about
them. Artistry refreshes those statistics (`PRAGMA optimize`, in full, for
tables that have none or have changed a lot) on open and on close; a
long-running process can call `Artistry.optimize` now and then. Until a
store's artifacts have statistics, SQLite may pass over an index and read
the kind in id order instead.

### Update (COW - default)

Creates a new version, supersedes the old:

```crystal
v1 = Artistry::Artifact.create("event", {title: "Draft", date: "2025-06-15"})
v2 = v1.update({title: "Final"})

v1.superseded?   # => true
v2.current?      # => true
v1.successor     # => v2
v2.history       # => [v1, v2]
```

### Update (Mutable)

Modifies in place:

```crystal
artifact.update!({title: "Changed"})
artifact.updated_at  # => unix milliseconds (Int64)
```

### Links

Links use `rel` (relation) to describe the relationship type:

```crystal
event = Artistry::Artifact.create("event", {title: "Meeting", date: "2025-06-15"})
person = Artistry::Artifact.create("person", {name: "Alice"})

# Create link with relation type
Artistry::Link.create(event, person, "organizer")
Artistry::Link.create(event, person, "attendee", {role: "presenter"})

# Query links by relation
Artistry::Link.from(event, "attendee")  # outgoing
Artistry::Link.to(person, "organizer")  # incoming

# Resolve linked artifacts
link = Artistry::Link.from(event).first
link.to   # => the person artifact
link.rel  # => "attendee"
```

### Tags

Tags are normalized — each unique tag string is stored once, then linked to artifacts via a junction table.

```crystal
# Tag an artifact
Artistry::Tag.tag(event, "security")
Artistry::Tag.tag(event, "mvp")

# Get tags for an artifact
Artistry::Tag.for(event)  # => [Tag("mvp"), Tag("security")]

# Find artifacts by tag
Artistry::Tag.artifacts("security")

# OR query - artifacts with any of the tags
Artistry::Tag.artifacts_any(["security", "mvp"])

# AND query - artifacts with all of the tags
Artistry::Tag.artifacts_all(["security", "mvp"])

# Replace all tags at once
Artistry::Tag.sync(event, ["v2", "released"])

# Remove a tag
Artistry::Tag.untag(event, "mvp")
```

### Transactions

Wrap multiple operations in a transaction for atomicity. The block yields a transaction context with convenient shortcuts:

```crystal
Artistry.transaction do |art|
  event = art.create("event", {title: "Meeting"})
  person = art.create("person", {name: "Alice"})
  art.link(event, person, "organizer")
  art.tag(event, "important")
end
# Auto-commits on success, auto-rollbacks on exception
```

The transaction context provides: `create`, `find`, `where`, `tag`, `untag`, `sync_tags`, `tags_for`, `link`, `unlink`, `links_from`, `links_to`, `rollback`, `commit`.

Call `art.rollback` for explicit rollback, or raise `DB::Rollback` for a silent rollback (no exception propagated). Class methods (`Artistry::Artifact.create`, etc.) also work inside the block and participate in the same transaction.

### Versioning Queries

```crystal
# Current versions only (default)
Artistry::Artifact.where("E")

# Include superseded versions
Artistry::Artifact.where("E", include_superseded: true)
```

## Tables

| Table | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `identity` | Global ID generator with `created_at` |
| `registry` | Kind registrations (`code`, `kind`, `plugin`, `description`, `symbol`, `version`) |
| `schema` | Versioned schemas with JSON and hash |
| `artifact` | All artifacts (JSON payload, COW tracking via `new_id`) |
| `link` | Cross-artifact references (`from_id`, `to_id`, `rel`, `data`) - CASCADE delete |
| `tag` | Unique tag names (`id`, `name`) |
| `tagging` | Junction table linking tags to artifacts - CASCADE delete both directions |
| `kind_index` | Which plugins asked for an index on a kind's fields (`code`, `fields`, `plugin`) |

## Technical Notes

- **Timestamps**: All `created_at`/`updated_at` fields are unix epoch milliseconds (Int64). Convert with `Time.unix_ms(ts)` in Crystal.
- **Foreign Keys**: FK constraints are enforced. Link and tagging FKs use `ON DELETE CASCADE` - deleting an artifact removes its links and taggings; deleting a tag removes its taggings.

def.body:
if @@owns_db && (db = @@db)
  refresh_statistics(db)
  db.close
end
@@db = nil
@@owns_db = false

class_methods.name: next_kind_seq
class_methods.doc:
Atomically allocate the next kind_seq for a given artifact code.

Inserts or increments the counter in `kind_counter`, then returns
the new sequence number. Thread-safe via SQLite's write lock.
class_methods.summary: Atomically allocate the next kind_seq for a given artifact code.

def.name: next_kind_seq
def.body:
c = conn
c.exec("INSERT INTO kind_counter (code, next_seq) VALUES (?, 1) ON CONFLICT(code) DO UPDATE SET next_seq = next_seq + 1", code)
(c.scalar("SELECT next_seq FROM kind_counter WHERE code = ?", code)).as(Int64)

def.name: open
def.body:
if @@db
  close
end
uri = path == ":memory:" ? "sqlite3:%3Amemory%3A" : "sqlite3://#{path}"
db = DB.open(uri)
db.exec("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
@@db = db
@@owns_db = true
Database.ensure_schema(db)
refresh_statistics(db)
db

class_methods.name: optimize
class_methods.doc:
Let SQLite refresh the statistics its query planner chooses indexes by
(`PRAGMA optimize`, which analyzes a table only when it has none or has
changed a lot, so it's quick otherwise). Without them it can pass over
an index. Runs on open and on close; a long-running process can call it
now and then too.
class_methods.summary: Let SQLite refresh the statistics its query planner chooses indexes by (PRAGMA optimize, which analyzes a table only when it has none or has changed a lot, so it's quick otherwise).

def.name: transaction
def.body:
begin
  db.using_connection do |conn|
    @@tx_connections[Fiber.current] = conn
    conn.transaction do |tx|
      yield Transaction.new(tx)
    end
  end
ensure
  @@tx_connections.delete(Fiber.current)
end

class_methods.name: find
class_methods.doc: Find by slug — supports both absolute (C99) and kind-relative (99C).
class_methods.summary: Find by slug — supports both absolute (C99) and kind-relative (99C).

def.name: find
def.body:
if match = slug.match(/^([A-Z]{1,2})(\d+)$/i)
  code = match[1].upcase
  id = match[2].to_i64?
  if id
    artifact = find(id)
    if artifact && (artifact.code == code)
      return artifact
    end
  end
end


if match = slug.match(/^(\d+)([A-Z]{1,2})$/i)
  seq = match[1].to_i64?
  code = match[2].upcase
  if seq
    return find_by_kind_seq(code, seq)
  end
end

nil

class_methods.doc: Query artifacts by code (current versions only by default)
class_methods.summary: Query artifacts by code (current versions only by default)

def.name: where
def.body:
results = [] of Artifact
sql = if include_superseded
  "SELECT #{FIND_COLUMNS} FROM artifact a\n               JOIN identity i ON a.id = i.id\n               WHERE a.code = ?\n               ORDER BY a.id"
else
  "SELECT #{FIND_COLUMNS} FROM artifact a\n               JOIN identity i ON a.id = i.id\n               WHERE a.code = ? AND a.new_id IS NULL\n               ORDER BY a.id"
end

Artistry.conn.query(sql, code) do |rs|
  rs.each do
    results << (Artifact.new(rs.read(Int64), rs.read(String), rs.read(Int32), JSON.parse(rs.read(String)), rs.read(String), rs.read(Int64), rs.read(::Union(Int64, ::Nil)), rs.read(::Union(Int64, ::Nil)), rs.read(::Union(Int64, ::Nil))))
  end
end
results

class_methods.name: where
class_methods.doc: Query with JSON field conditions (current versions only by default)
class_methods.summary: Query with JSON field conditions (current versions only by default)

def.name: where
def.body:
if conditions.empty?
  return where(code, include_superseded)
end

where_clauses = ["a.code = ?"]
if include_superseded
else
  where_clauses << "a.new_id IS NULL"
end
params = [code] of DB::Any

conditions.each do |key, value|
  where_clauses << "json_extract(a.data, '$.#{key}') = ?"
  params << value
end

sql = "  SELECT #{FIND_COLUMNS}\n  FROM artifact a\n  JOIN identity i ON a.id = i.id\n  WHERE #{where_clauses.join(" AND ")}\n  ORDER BY a.id"

results = [] of Artifact
Artistry.conn.query(sql, args: params) do |rs|
  rs.each do
    results << (Artifact.new(rs.read(Int64), rs.read(String), rs.read(Int32), JSON.parse(rs.read(String)), rs.read(String), rs.read(Int64), rs.read(::Union(Int64, ::Nil)), rs.read(::Union(Int64, ::Nil)), rs.read(::Union(Int64, ::Nil))))
  end
end
results

instance_methods.name: hash
instance_methods.doc:
Generates an `UInt64` hash value for this object.

This method must have the property that `a == b` implies `a.hash == b.hash`.

The hash value is used along with `==` by the `Hash` class to determine if two objects
reference the same hash key.

Subclasses must not override this method. Instead, they must define `hash(hasher)`,
though usually the macro `def_hash` can be used to generate this method.
instance_methods.summary: Generates an UInt64 hash value for this object.

instance_methods.name: history
instance_methods.doc: Get the full history chain (oldest first)

def.name: history
def.body:
root = self
loop do

  prev = Artistry.conn.query_one?("SELECT id FROM artifact WHERE new_id = ?", root.id, as: Int64)
  if prev
  else
    break
  end
  prev_artifact = Artifact.find(prev)
  if prev_artifact
  else
    break
  end
  root = prev_artifact
end


chain = [root]
current = root
while current.superseded?
  next_version = current.successor
  if next_version
  else
    break
  end
  chain << next_version
  current = next_version
end
chain

def.name: update
def.body:
if superseded?
  raise("Cannot update superseded artifact (use .latest.update)")
end

db = Artistry.conn


current_version = db.query_one?("SELECT version FROM registry WHERE code = ?", code, as: Int32)
if current_version
else
  raise("Unknown artifact code: #{code}")
end


new_json = (JSON.parse(new_data.to_json)).as_h
merged = data.as_h.merge(new_json)
merged_parsed = JSON.parse(merged.to_json)


schema = Registry.get_schema(code, current_version)
if schema
  merged_parsed = Validator.apply_defaults(merged_parsed, schema)
  Validator.validate(merged_parsed, schema)
end

data_json = merged_parsed.to_json
data_hash = Artifact.hash_data(data_json)


seq = Artistry.next_kind_seq(code)
db.exec("INSERT INTO identity (code, kind_seq) VALUES (?, ?)", code, seq)
new_id = (db.scalar("SELECT last_insert_rowid()")).as(Int64)


db.exec("INSERT INTO artifact (id, code, version, data, hash) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)", new_id, code, current_version, data_json, data_hash)


db.exec("UPDATE artifact SET new_id = ? WHERE id = ?", new_id, id)

new_created_at = db.query_one("SELECT created_at FROM identity WHERE id = ?", new_id, as: Int64)

Artifact.new(new_id, code, current_version, merged_parsed, data_hash, new_created_at, kind_seq: seq)

instance_methods.name: update!
instance_methods.doc: Mutable update - modifies in place, sets updated_at
instance_methods.summary: Mutable update - modifies in place, sets updated_at

def.name: update!
def.body:
db = Artistry.conn


current_version = db.query_one?("SELECT version FROM registry WHERE code = ?", code, as: Int32)
if current_version
else
  raise("Unknown artifact code: #{code}")
end


new_json = (JSON.parse(new_data.to_json)).as_h
merged = data.as_h.merge(new_json)
merged_parsed = JSON.parse(merged.to_json)


schema = Registry.get_schema(code, current_version)
if schema
  merged_parsed = Validator.apply_defaults(merged_parsed, schema)
  Validator.validate(merged_parsed, schema)
end

data_json = merged_parsed.to_json
data_hash = Artifact.hash_data(data_json)
now = Artifact.now_ms

db.exec("UPDATE artifact SET data = ?, version = ?, hash = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?", data_json, current_version, data_hash, now, id)

Artifact.new(id, code, current_version, merged_parsed, data_hash, created_at, new_id, now, kind_seq)

constants.name: SCHEMA
constants.value:
"  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS identity (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    code TEXT,
    kind_seq INTEGER,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (cast((julianday('now') - 2440587.5) * 86400000 as integer))
  );

  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kind_counter (
    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    next_seq INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
  );

  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS registry (
    code TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    plugin TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    symbol TEXT,
    version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
    UNIQUE(plugin, kind)
  );

  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema (
    code TEXT NOT NULL,
    version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    json TEXT NOT NULL,
    hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (cast((julianday('now') - 2440587.5) * 86400000 as integer)),
    PRIMARY KEY (code, version),
    FOREIGN KEY (code) REFERENCES registry(code)
  );

  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS artifact (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    code TEXT NOT NULL,
    version INTEGER NOT NULL,
    data JSON NOT NULL,
    hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    new_id INTEGER REFERENCES identity(id),
    updated_at INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (id) REFERENCES identity(id),
    FOREIGN KEY (code, version) REFERENCES schema(code, version)
  );

  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_artifact_code ON artifact(code);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_artifact_new_id ON artifact(new_id) WHERE new_id IS NOT NULL;

  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS kind_index (
    code TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES registry(code),
    fields TEXT NOT NULL,
    plugin TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (code, fields, plugin)
  ) WITHOUT ROWID;

  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS link (
    from_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES identity(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    to_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES identity(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    rel TEXT NOT NULL,
    data JSON,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (cast((julianday('now') - 2440587.5) * 86400000 as integer)),
    PRIMARY KEY (from_id, to_id, rel)
  );

  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tag (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (cast((julianday('now') - 2440587.5) * 86400000 as integer))
  );

  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tagging (
    tag_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES tag(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    artifact_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES identity(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT (cast((julianday('now') - 2440587.5) * 86400000 as integer)),
    PRIMARY KEY (tag_id, artifact_id)
  );

def.name: ensure_schema

(SCHEMA.split(";")).each do |stmt|
  stmt = stmt.strip
  if stmt.empty?
    next
  end
  db.exec(stmt)
end




existing = db.query_all("SELECT name FROM pragma_table_info('identity')", as: String)
{"code" => "TEXT", "kind_seq" => "INTEGER"}.each do |column, type|
  if existing.includes?(column)
  else
    db.exec("ALTER TABLE identity ADD COLUMN #{column} #{type}")
  end
end


db.exec("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_identity_kind_seq ON identity(code, kind_seq)")





new_id_index = db.query_one?("SELECT sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'index' AND name = 'idx_artifact_new_id'", as: String)
if new_id_index && !(new_id_index.includes?("WHERE"))
  db.exec("DROP INDEX idx_artifact_new_id")

`InvalidIndex`.

class_methods.name: allocate_code
class_methods.doc:
Allocate a free one- or two-letter code for a kind name.

Tries the first letter, then the first letter followed by each later
letter of the name, then the first letter followed by A-Z. Codes are
capped at two letters because slugs ("C42", "42C") are parsed that way.
class_methods.summary: Allocate a free one- or two-letter code for a kind name.

def.name: allocate_code
def.body:
letters = kind.upcase.gsub(/[^A-Z]/, "")
if letters.empty?
  raise(Error.new("Cannot allocate a code for kind #{kind.inspect}: it has no letters"))
end

first = letters[0]
candidates = [first.to_s]
letters[1..].each_char do |c| candidates << "#{first}#{c}" end
('A'..'Z').each do |c| candidates << "#{first}#{c}" end

candidates.uniq.each do |candidate|
  exists = db.query_one?("SELECT 1 FROM registry WHERE code = ?", candidate, as: Int32)
  if exists
  else
    return candidate
  end
end

raise(Error.new("No free code for kind #{kind.inspect}: all codes starting with #{first} are taken (declare one with code:)"))

class_methods.name: register
class_methods.doc:
Register a new artifact kind. Returns the assigned code.
Schema is a JSON Schema as any JSON-serializable value. Raises
`InvalidSchema` if it can't be parsed, so it fails here rather than
on every create.
`index` lists the indexes this plugin asks for on the kind, as
`add_index` does: each entry a field or an ordered list of fields
(`["title", ["voice", "bit"]]`). Leaving one out later doesn't drop it;
`drop_index` does.

`code` declares the kind's code (one or two uppercase letters) so it
doesn't depend on registration order. Without it, a code is allocated
from the kind name. Raises `InvalidCode`, `CodeConflict` (another kind
owns the code) or `CodeMismatch` (this kind is already registered
under a different code).
class_methods.summary: Register a new artifact kind.
class_methods.args_string: (kind : String, plugin : String, schema, description : String | Nil = nil, symbol : String | Nil = nil, index : Array = [] of String, code : String | Nil = nil) : String
class_methods.args_html: (kind : String, plugin : String, schema, description : String | Nil = nil, symbol : String | Nil = nil, index : Array = [] of String, code : String | Nil = nil) : String

def.name: register
def.body:
db = Artistry.conn
kind = kind.downcase
plugin = plugin.downcase
declared = code
if declared && !(CODE_FORMAT.matches?(declared))
  raise(InvalidCode.new(declared))
end
check_schema(plugin, kind, schema)


existing = db.query_one?("SELECT code, version FROM registry WHERE plugin = ? AND kind = ?", plugin, kind, as: {String, Int32})

if existing
  code, current_version = existing
  if declared && (declared != code)
    raise(CodeMismatch.new(plugin, kind, code, declared))
  end


  schema_json = normalize_schema(schema)
  schema_hash = hash_schema(schema_json)

  last_hash = db.query_one?("SELECT hash FROM schema WHERE code = ? AND version = ?", code, current_version, as: String)

  if last_hash != schema_hash
    new_version = current_version + 1
    db.exec("UPDATE registry SET version = ? WHERE code = ?", new_version, code)
    db.exec("INSERT INTO schema (code, version, json, hash) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", code, new_version, schema_json, schema_hash)
  end

  index.each do |fields| add_index(code, fields, plugin: plugin) end

  return code
end


code = if declared
  if owner = db.query_one?("SELECT plugin, kind FROM registry WHERE code = ?", declared, as: {String, String})
    raise(CodeConflict.new(declared, plugin, kind, owner[0], owner[1]))
  end
  declared
else
  allocate_code(db, kind)
end

db.exec("INSERT INTO registry (code, kind, plugin, description, symbol, version) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 1)", code, kind, plugin, description, symbol)

schema_json = normalize_schema(schema)
schema_hash = hash_schema(schema_json)

db.exec("INSERT INTO schema (code, version, json, hash) VALUES (?, 1, ?, ?)", code, schema_json, schema_hash)

index.each do |fields| add_index(code, fields, plugin: plugin) end

code
